was: Private campground ('East Fork Campground and Horse Hotel') on the East Fork of the Greenbrier River at Durbin (Pocahontas Co); the operator notes horses are kept away from the campground. Full-hookup (30-amp) RV sites with pull-thrus plus tent sites, cabin, lodge and group area; open ~Apr-Oct, ~$56/night. Tent sites line the riverbank; RV sites are mixed (some riverfront, some set back). --Claude  Per the operator (2026): 30-amp full hookups, municipal water, a dump station, a camp store, a bathhouse with hot showers, and a pavilion and playground; pet friendly. Book via CampLife or by phone (days only). The RV sites are grass with gravel pads in an open field along the river. Reviews (2020-26) consistently call it spotless, with very accommodating owners, and note that many guests are long-stay horse campers. The Durbin Rocket steam-excursion depot is at the entrance. There's no cell on any carrier, but the campground Wi-Fi handles email. Durbin has few services, so arrive stocked. Tubing and kayaking on the East Fork are possible when the river level allows. --Claude
note: Campground and horse hotel on the East Fork of the Greenbrier River at Durbin (Pocahontas County), bordering 300,000 acres of the Monongahela National Forest and open April 1 to October 31.  RV sites have 30-amp power and water, some with full hookups, some pull-through and some on the river; there are also tent sites, two cabins and a six-bedroom lodge across the road.  There are hot showers, municipal water, a dump station, a camp store, a pavilion and a playground; horses stay in stalls, never at the campsites.  The Durbin Rocket excursion train's depot is at the entrance, and there is no cell service, but the campground Wi-Fi handles email. --Claude
